proof.criterion: Finding 1: a soft setRole refused at startup no longer costs the session its role for the life of the process, and a refusal that repeats is still retried.
proof.surface: The committed dist/envoy-channel.js run as Claude Code runs it, against a real nats-server with JetStream and an Envoy listener built from this tree, with a proxy in front of the listener that answers 503 to the first two POSTs of /v1/roles/set and forwards everything else.
proof.command: a throwaway probe, /tmp/role-round2-probe.sh (not in the tree), case one
proof.observed: After startup: the session alive and already holding — no, precisely: alive=yes with one stderr line, 'could not restore the role from <…> (POST …/v1/roles/set failed with 503: injected listener outage); the next heartbeat retries'. The proxy recorded refusals=2, so the first heartbeat's retry was refused as well, and the listener named the session holder of the role after the third claim. Two refusals, not one, is the point: `transferRole` clears the queued retry only once `restoreRole` resolves, so a single failure would pass even if the retry were one-shot.

Before this round, the catch wrote the same line and nothing ever re-ran the claim — the unit row 'a role claim that fails at startup still starts the session, and the next heartbeat takes the role back' fails against that code.

reviewFindings: 1 (blocking) — fixed. The startup catch sets `roleTransferFrom = identity.id`, so the heartbeat's existing `transferRole` → `restoreRole` path re-runs the claim, and because `transferRole` clears the queue only after `restoreRole` resolves, a repeated failure stays queued. A role file that cannot be parsed is deliberately not queued: no later read of the same bytes succeeds, and a transfer that threw every tick would end each one before its interests reconciliation. The stderr line says which case it was.

2 (blocking) — fixed. `reassertRole`'s holder-confirmed branch touches the record through the new `touchStateFile`. A timestamp touch, not a rewrite, on the architect's instruction: the content has not changed, and an atomic rewrite would drop a temporary file into `roles/` every two minutes — which is also why the three existing `readdir(roles)` assertions the first attempt had to move after `shutdown()` are back where they were, untouched.

3 (minor) — fixed. `MD_VIEWPORT_QUERY` is `(min-width: 48rem)` and its comment says why the unit matters. Only that token changed: `COMPACT_VIEWPORT_QUERY` and `PHONE_VIEWPORT_QUERY` carry the same px-against-rem mismatch and are left alone, as the reviewer asked, as the pull request's one Fast-follow line.

Threads — the five the reviewer named as accepted are resolved by node id. The reviewer also opened three threads for this round's findings, which it did not name: each has one disposition reply and is resolved. PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v9duc, which the reviewer asked to leave open, is answered and resolved too, on the architect's instruction that it stays open only until finding 3 is in the head — which this head carries.

packages/claude-envoy/src/session-identity.ts — the role sweep's doc comment, which reasoned about a record nothing touches

trickyParts: The touch has to be a touch. A rewrite through `writePersistedRole` is atomic — a temporary file in `roles/` renamed over the record — so every two minutes a listing of that directory could catch the temporary file, which is what made three existing assertions flake until they were moved after shutdown. `touchStateFile` writes nothing and leaves nothing beside the record, and those three assertions are back in their original places.

An unparseable role file is not queued for retry. It is the one failure a later read of the same bytes cannot fix, and a `transferRole` that threw on every tick would end each heartbeat before `syncRegisteredInterests`.
openQuestions: One interaction of the two fixes, found by the first version of the probe and reported to the architect rather than fixed, because this round was scoped to the three findings: a role record already older than thirty days whose startup claim is refused is deleted by the startup sweep, which runs after the restore, before the queued retry can use it. The record is then gone and the retry finds nothing. It needs both an aged record and a transient listener failure in the same startup, the session can still claim the role itself through `rememberRole`, and either fix (sweeping before the restore, or skipping the role sweep while a retry is queued) is a change the architect asked not to make this round. Proven incidentally: the probe's first version, which aged the record and refused the claim in one run, ended with the record deleted and the role unheld.
discoveredComplexity: A worker container's /home is not durable within a session: `nats-server`, installed into GOPATH's bin earlier in this issue and used by three smoke runs, was gone by this round, and the smoke failed with `nats-server: command not found` through a listener that then died of `nats: no servers available`. It is reinstalled at /legion/scratch/bin, on the issue volume, which the rest of the rig already uses. A smoke or probe that needs a tool should look there first.

The browser rig needs `@legion/contracts` built (`cd packages/contracts && bun run build`, 0.13 s) before Playwright loads the specs, and a run killed by a command deadline leaves its five harness listeners holding their ports; both cost a run each in earlier rounds and are in the retro learning already queued.
